chunks: Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād narrated from Ibn ʿAbbād who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said: A good turn is not considered a good turn except with one who possesses honor or religion.

key_terms.الصَّنِيعَةُ: A good turn, favor, or deed of kindness

ai.seo_question: What conditions must be met for a favor to be considered a true good turn in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a favor is only truly recognized as a 'good turn' (sani'ah) when bestowed upon one of 'quality' (ahl al-hasb), specifically those possessing noble lineage or deep piety. This hadith, found in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, underscores the Shia emphasis on the spiritual and social merit of the recipient, linking the efficacy of charity to the recipient's worthiness rather than merely the act itself. It reflects the broader scholarly understanding that 'hasb' encompasses both ancestral honor and personal religious standing, ensuring the deed is preserved and valued.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 4.Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād narrated from Ibn ʿAbbād who said, “
AbūʿAbdillāh (a) said, ‘A good turn is not considered a good turn except with one who possesses honor or religion.’”
